key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match the expressivity of multi-qubit circuits with the same encoding budget, but their first-order training is much harder because all parameters become phase-locked on the Bloch sphere.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning, increasing circuit depth instead of width can preserve function class while sharply degrading optimization reliability, so architecture choice must consider trainability as well as expressivity.
method: Analyzed Fourier-series expressivity of angle-encoded variational circuits with encoding budget E.
Proved the serial single-qubit circuit has at most 2E+2 tangent directions, while a comparable two-qubit control generically has at least 6E+6.
Benchmarked gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg–Marquardt on exact flat-spectrum targets and three real-world time series.
evidence_signal: At E=32 on the exact loss, the serial circuit converged in 3/53/83 runs under gradient descent/Adam/Levenberg–Marquardt, versus 99/100/100 for the two-qubit control; on real data it also showed worse or only matched held-out error depending on optimizer.
watch_item: The advantage of the wider control model is demonstrated under matched encoding budget and parameter-count settings, so results may depend on optimizer choice, initialization, and the specific one-dimensional encoding regime.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
